meta.description: Total Recall skill invocation analysis across 6 JSONL transcript files from two Claude Code project directories

trigger.description: User injected a queue message mid-session while AI was already searching the filesystem for media files
trigger.underlying_need: Confirm location of personal media collection (classic cartoons) using cross-session memory
trigger.user_message_summary: use /total-recall to find where they are

query.skill_args: looney tunes warner brothers cartoons golden collection ranked videos
query.notes: AI had already found ~/Desktop/Video/Golden Collection/ranked via direct filesystem traversal before TR search completed. No CLI commands recorded in the excerpt - skill may have executed but the filesystem discovery preempted it.

results.notes: AI explicitly noted it had found the directory ~/Desktop/Video/Golden Collection/ranked before the skill concluded. The TR results (if any) were redundant. Outcome was filesystem-driven, not TR-driven.

delivery.description: AI confirmed the media directory location via direct filesystem listing; TR was a secondary confirmation that was superseded

aftermath.action_taken: AI continued with the original task (browsing/ranking the media files) using the already-found directory path

invocations.notes: Interesting case where the AI found the answer before TR completed. The queue injection pattern caused TR to run in parallel with filesystem exploration rather than as a primary lookup.

trigger.description: User opened session with a direct TR request as the primary task
trigger.underlying_need: Locate prior work and repo for a personal creative side project (bootleg novelty hats based on a fiction franchise)
trigger.user_message_summary: I had previously been working on some [franchise] hats but i don't know where i had all the information / repo can you find it /total-recall?

cli_commands.command: contextify search '"[franchise] [character]" AND (hat OR hats OR cap OR caps OR headgear)' --days 365 --limit 20 --snippet-tokens 50 --json
cli_commands.description: First search: exact phrase for franchise + headgear synonyms

cli_commands.command: contextify search '"[franchise]" OR "[abbreviation]" OR "bootleg hats" OR "[character] hats"' --days 365 --limit 20 --snippet-tokens 50 --json
cli_commands.description: Second search: broader OR query after first returned only passing references

results.notes: First query returned 2 results, both from an administration-type project referencing the creative project only in passing (describing it as a personal side-project to be archived). AI correctly characterized these as insufficient and ran a broader second query.

delivery.description: AI reported search results inline and escalated to broader search strategy

aftermath.action_taken: Broader follow-up search executed; transcript excerpt ends before final resolution - unclear if the project/repo was ultimately located

invocations.notes: Classic cross-session continuity use case. The creative project predated or existed outside the indexed transcript window. The initial search found administrative context about the project but not the actual project work.

trigger.description: User opened session requesting a TR-driven audit of recent work in a personal tooling project and cross-machine cloud sync verification
trigger.underlying_need: Verify what work had been done in a personal CLI tooling project and whether changes had synced across machines
trigger.user_message_summary: Read the recent work in [personal tooling project] and verify cross-machine cloud sync

cli_commands.command: contextify search '"cli-ai-setup" OR skill* OR hook* OR agent*' --days 7 --limit 10 --snippet-tokens 50 --json
cli_commands.description: Initial FTS search - FAILED with FTS5 hyphen tokenization error
cli_commands.error: no such column: ai (FTS5 tokenized 'cli-ai-setup' on hyphens, 'ai' interpreted as column name)

cli_commands.description: List projects to get UUID for the personal tooling project
Project-scoped activity query using explicit UUID (workaround for FTS error and --project name flag bug)

results.notes: Found 2 recent sessions from 2026-03-15: a personal tooling migration session and a utility implementation session. Machine provenance could not be determined - no hostname or device_id field in the CLI data model. Also hit two bugs: FTS5 hyphen tokenization error and --project flag defaulting to cwd project rather than looking up by name.

delivery.description: Full audit report written to /tmp/ with frank assessment that machine provenance is indeterminate. AI explicitly stated 'the honest answer is I can't tell which machine produced any entry'.

aftermath.action_taken: Report delivered with honest capability limitation documented. Session continued with other tasks.
aftermath.limitation_documented: No hostname or device_id field in CLI data model; cross-machine attribution is not possible with current schema

bugs_encountered.description: FTS5 splits hyphenated terms on hyphens; 'cli-ai-setup' becomes tokens [cli, ai, setup], and 'ai' is interpreted as a column reference
bugs_encountered.workaround: Switched from FTS search to project-scoped contextify activity with explicit UUID

bugs_encountered.description: contextify activity --project [name] defaulted to cwd project (misc) instead of looking up by name
bugs_encountered.workaround: Used --project-id with explicit UUID from contextify projects --json output

invocations.notes: First of two invocations in this session. Notable for exposing two CLI bugs and for the AI's honest provenance limitation assessment rather than fabricating machine attribution.

trigger.underlying_need: Recover original build methodology for a macOS Finder toolbar app with custom icon from prior session history
trigger.user_message_summary: the methodology may actually be in /total-recall

query.notes: Specific CLI commands not recorded in available excerpt. AI reported negative result.

results.notes: No results found. AI concluded: 'No luck finding the original methodology in Total Recall. The creation predates the indexed history.' Negative proof - the work predated the transcript indexing window.

delivery.description: Brief inline report of negative result with explanation that the work predates indexed history

aftermath.action_taken: Session continued without the original methodology; presumably reconstructed or approached differently

invocations.notes: Second invocation in this session. A clean negative-proof case: TR correctly reported no results rather than returning false positives. The creation predated the indexed transcript window.

trigger.description: User asked whether the spec for a task (bl-331) had been derived from TR. When AI said no, user requested TR be run to recover prior design discussions before finalizing the spec.
trigger.underlying_need: Recover prior user design discussions about an AI-evaluated focus feature to ensure valuable prior thinking was incorporated into the task spec
trigger.user_message_summary: was the spec for 331 partly derived from using /total-recall to look for past discussion about this? i want to make sure any valuable information from my pining for this previously makes its way into whatever you're planning

query.skill_args: AI-evaluated focus changes, focus should be intelligent, auto-advance focus wrong project

cli_commands.command: contextify search 'focus AND (intelligent OR smart OR AI OR evaluate* OR reason* OR context*)' --project . --days 365 --limit 20 --snippet-tokens 50 --json
cli_commands.description: Primary search for AI-evaluated focus discussions in the bloon project
Fetched surrounding context for a high-value Feb 11 entry about AI-driven task transitions

high_value_hits.description: Prior discussion specifically about AI-evaluated focus transitions
Rich discussion about AI-driven task transitions with interactive confirmation, candidate presentation with reasoning, hierarchy-aware rules

results.notes: 298 total results. AI correctly identified the Feb 11 discussion as the most valuable hit and fetched context around entry 45c84f41 to recover the full prior design discussion.

delivery.description: AI summarized the recovered design discussion and immediately applied it to update the bl-331 task spec

aftermath.action_taken: bl-331 task spec updated with 4 key elements recovered from prior discussions
spec_additions: Interactive confirmation before closing a focus item (not silent auto-advance)
Candidate presentation with reasoning (AI shows options and explains why)
Hierarchy-aware rules (leaf/atomic steps auto-advance; substantial work prompts user)
Clarification that this is primarily an AI behavior change, not CLI plumbing
aftermath.compact_summary_reference: Context compaction summary at line 1144 explicitly noted 'prior Feb 11 discussion found via Total Recall'

invocations.notes: Highest-impact invocation in the batch. TR recovered a design discussion from 5+ weeks prior that materially changed a task spec. The user's explicit goal ('make sure valuable information makes its way in') was fully satisfied. The compact summary itself referenced TR as a key source, confirming the AI internalized the findings.

trigger.description: During debugging of a spurious project created with a 'cc-' prefix in the task manager, user asked TR to find when the incident occurred and what commands had been run
trigger.underlying_need: Incident forensics: determine when and how an AI session created a spurious prefixed project entry in the task management tool
trigger.user_message_summary: can you use /total-recall to look for when this happened, look for 'cc-' and see how we might be able to add context somewhere or maybe a command's output like deleting a project, might get a hint toward it

query.skill_args: search for "cc-" bloon project creation contextify-cloud, when did an AI create or attempt to create a cc- prefixed project in bloon, and what commands were run

cli_commands.command: contextify search '"cc-" AND (bloon OR prefix OR task)' --days 365 --limit 15 --snippet-tokens 80 --json

cli_commands.description: Attempted context fetch around a result entry - FAILED with sibling tool call error

results.notes: 80 total results but none specifically about the cc- project creation event. Results contained 'cc' as abbreviation for Claude Code, entry IDs starting with 'cc', filenames with 'cc' prefix, and tangential cloud repo setup references - none pinpointed the specific spurious project creation incident.

delivery.description: AI reported the search results and their limitations inline; pivoted to checking bloon project list directly

aftermath.action_taken: AI attempted bloon project list to check if cc- project still exists; Python parsing errored. Context fetch of a result also errored. Investigation concluded without finding the specific creation event.

bugs_encountered.description: bloon project list --json | python3 filter raised AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'lower' because data was list of dicts not strings
contextify context call returned sibling tool call errored

invocations.notes: Earliest session in the batch (2026-03-01). A true incident forensics use case that returned high volume (80 results) but low signal - the specific event was not indexed or occurred in a session predating the index window. The 'cc-' prefix was too common a substring to isolate the creation event. Illustrates a precision limitation when searching for short or common token patterns.

bugs_surfaced: FTS5 hyphen tokenization: hyphenated terms split on hyphens causing column-not-found errors
--project flag defaulting to cwd project instead of looking up by name
Python parsing error in bloon project list filter (dict vs string)
Sibling tool call error on contextify context fetch
